title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 90–93): over a base S_0 where 2 is invertible (presumably Z[1/2] or a variant), Grothendieck compares 'Legendre' and 'Jacobi' rigidifications of elliptic curves. U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} is the λ-line, the modular scheme for ordered level-2 data. D_3 ≅ S_3 = GL_2(F_2) is the anharmonic group acting on it, and sg: D_3 → {±1} is the sign character. The previous page computes how the modular action T_{g,λ} of D_3 × μ_4 acts on sections of O(1), O(2) and a twisted O(2) on the λ-line (formulas 51–53). On the subgroup D'_3 = {(g,λ) : λ^2 = sg(g)} the factors collapse to the canonical character χ_4 : D'_3 → μ_4, using D'_3^ab ≅ μ_4. As an abstract group D'_3 has order 12: (g,λ) ↦ λ is onto μ_4 with kernel A_3 ≅ Z/3. So D'_3 ≅ Z/3 ⋊ Z/4, the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group Dic_3. It is a quotient of SL_2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6.

This page first says when these formulas are most useful. That is when one works over S̃_0 = μ_4^* (the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity over S_0, i.e. adjoining i), and the structures are Legendre–Jacobi structures. In that setting the modular scheme U_{0,3} ×_{S_0} μ_4^* over S_0 is simply U_{0,3} base-changed to S̃_0 (Grothendieck's '!' marks this tautology). The modular group D_3 × μ_4 is replaced by D'_3 over S̃_0. The last line names a further group, read here (unsure) as Z_8 or μ_8, as 'its inverse image on S̃_0'. This fits the 8th roots of unity familiar from theta transformation formulas.

Second paragraph, a programme. Define a 'Jacobi pinning of level 4 relative to level 2' as follows. Let J_E = (₂E)^*, the finite étale degree-3 cover of nonzero 2-torsion points P_1, P_2, P_3. The pinning is a section of ₄E → ₂E over J_E, i.e. a choice of halves ξ_i with 2ξ_i = P_i. On each geometric fibre it must satisfy ξ_1 + ξ_2 + ξ_3 = 0. Since P_1 + P_2 + P_3 = 0, the sum ξ_1 + ξ_2 + ξ_3 is automatically 2-torsion. The condition therefore cuts the 4^3 = 64 choices down to 16, a torsor under a subgroup of (₂E)^3. Grothendieck then wants to show that such a pinning canonically defines a Legendre pinning: an ordered level-2 structure together with a trivialisation of the quadratic-twist ambiguity, so that the curve is literally y^2 = x(x−1)(x−λ).

Classically this is the passage from the Legendre modulus λ to Jacobi's modulus k with k^2 = λ, k'^2 = 1−λ. The halving criterion for (e_i, 0) requires the square roots of (e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k), namely of λ, 1−λ and −λ(1−λ). These involve √−1, which explains the appearance of μ_4. The next page then treats the twist via μ_2-torsors: choose T with T^{⊗2} ≃ T_{Σ,t}, and an isomorphism μ_4^♮ ≃ ω_J.

ideas.what: Modular group D'_3 = {(g,λ) ∈ S_3 × μ_4 : λ^2 = sg(g)}, with abelianisation μ_4 and canonical character χ_4, acting on Legendre/Jacobi moduli over Z[1/2, i]
ideas.modern_name: Dicyclic group Dic_3 as a quotient of SL_2(Z); the automorphy character relating theta/Legendre data to Γ(2)–Γ(4) moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Jacobi, Hermite theta transformation); scheme-theoretic level structures by Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Jacobi pinning of level 4 relative to level 2: halves ξ_i of the three nonzero 2-torsion points with ξ_1 + ξ_2 + ξ_3 = 0, defined as a section of ₄E → ₂E over J_E = (₂E)^*
ideas.modern_name: Intermediate level structure between Γ(2) and Γ(4) (Jacobi modulus k, k' with k^2 = λ); rigidifies the quadratic twist of the Legendre form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Jacobi/Legendre theory; modern treatment implicit in Katz–Mazur and Igusa

ideas.what: Identification U_{0,3} ×_{S_0} μ_4^* = U_{0,3, S̃_0} after base change to S̃_0 = μ_4^*
ideas.modern_name: Base change of the λ-line to Z[1/2, i]

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to show that a Jacobi relative level-4 pinning canonically determines a Legendre pinning, including the trivialisation of the twist, in a fully functorial way over any base with 2 invertible, with explicit equivariance under Dic_3 and μ_8. Classically this is known, but a clean stack-theoretic statement of exactly this form is not standard in the literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: Il faut maintenant définir les épinglages de Jacobi d'échelon 4 relatifs sur l'échelon 2 ... et montrer comment un tel épinglage définit canoniquement un épinglage de Legendre.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor expository gap at most: it gives a canonical moduli interpretation of the Legendre and Jacobi normal forms. Such interpretations are relevant to explicit models of modular stacks and to dessins/λ-line arithmetic, but are largely folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but classical scheme-theoretic reworking of the Legendre/Jacobi normal forms and their automorphy characters. The order-12 dicyclic group with abelianisation μ_4 is a nice detail but well known in substance. No genuinely new result appears on the page.
